subsystems.name: Optical pulse sensor
subsystems.role: reads heart rate and its beat-to-beat variation from blood flow under the skin.

subsystems.name: Temperature sensor
subsystems.role: tracks skin temperature through the night; the finger gives a steadier reading than the wrist.

subsystems.name: Motion sensor
subsystems.role: detects movement and orientation so sleep and activity can be separated.

subsystems.name: Electronics and battery
subsystems.role: runs the sensors and stores or streams the data.
parts: charging contacts or wireless charging coil

subsystems.name: Shell and seal
subsystems.role: keeps water and sweat out while staying comfortable for weeks on end.

subsystems.name: Algorithms and app
subsystems.role: turn raw signals into sleep stages, readiness and illness alerts.

buildSteps.title: Design the form
buildSteps.detail: The ring must fit fingers from size 6 to 13 while holding LEDs, battery and antennas in a few cubic centimetres.

buildSteps.title: Build the sensor module
buildSteps.detail: LEDs, photodiodes and thermistors are mounted on a flexible circuit that curves around the inner band.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the electronics
buildSteps.detail: Microcontroller, radio and battery are stacked inside the shell and connected to the sensor flex.

buildSteps.title: Seal and finish
buildSteps.detail: The shell is bonded and sealed so the ring survives showers, swimming and daily wear.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Each unit's optical readings are checked against reference signals so measurements are comparable between rings.

buildSteps.title: Train the models
buildSteps.detail: Sleep and recovery algorithms are fitted to data from users wearing the ring alongside lab sleep studies; this is the most expensive part.

buildSteps.title: Validate and ship
buildSteps.detail: Accuracy is tested against reference instruments, then the ring is paired with its app and released.

buildSteps.title: Update over the air
buildSteps.detail: Firmware and scoring models are refined for years after purchase, as the device is worn every night.

prerequisites.why: commercial LEDs and photodiodes are now small and efficient enough to run in a ring.
sensors must run for several days between charges from a very small battery.
the battery sets how small the ring can be and how long it lasts.
scoring agrees reasonably with lab sleep studies but is not a clinical measurement.
the ring is worn 24 hours a day against skin.

pathway.milestone: mass-market rings scoring sleep, heart rate variability and temperature trends
pathway.unlocks: continuous personal health data without a screen or daily charging routine.

pathway.milestone: regulatory clearance for specific clinical claims such as irregular-rhythm notification
pathway.unlocks: ring data becoming usable in medical care rather than only wellness.
long-term cardiovascular monitoring from a finger.

pathway.milestone: non-invasive sensing of blood analytes such as glucose
pathway.unlocks: continuous metabolic monitoring without skin pricks, if accuracy can be proven.
